subject: Decision criteria, tie-breakers and escalation path
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + two clarifying questions on decision criteria

Hi Samira / Paul —

Thanks again for your time on today’s demo. I promised a short recap and a couple concrete questions so we can align the next steps with the right stakeholders on your side. Attaching the latency_cost_matrix.xlsx we referenced.

What I heard as the high-level priorities:
- Latency (user-facing inference) is primary — you need consistent p95 numbers for interactive flows.
- Cost constraints for initial pilot: narrow band that guides whether we recommend Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Compliance (SOC 2) and data residency are gating for PHI flows.

Two clarifying questions to help us map the buying path and prepare the procurement package:
1) Decision thresholds: what counts as a pass/fail for latency? e.g., is p95 generation <=120ms acceptable, or do you need something tighter (<=80–100ms)?
2) Deployment preference: do you have a hard requirement for Private (VPC/on-prem) for production PHI data, or would Dedicated reserved capacity in a customer VPC be acceptable?

If you can confirm those two items and the list of internal stakeholders who need to sign off (economic buyer, legal, procurement, IT/security), we’ll prepare a short decision memo and an updated SOW to get into your procurement queue.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm thresholds and stakeholders by Wed 11/11
- If you want a technical deep-dive, we can schedule Karthik for a 60-minute call next week to walk latency/cost tradeoffs and deployment options

Attachments: latency_cost_matrix.xlsx (cost/latency scenarios)

Thanks — Jordan

Subject: Re: Quick recap + two clarifying questions on decision criteria

Jordan — thanks for the crisp recap and for the attachment. Short answers below and a couple of asks from procurement.

1) Latency thresholds: for our main clinician UI we are targeting p95 end-to-end generation <=120ms for typical prompts (avg ~500 tokens); we can tolerate up to 160ms for larger documents in background jobs. If you can show consistently under 120ms p95 in a dedicated setup, that’s the primary checkbox for the UX owners.

2) Deployment: for pilot data that is de-identified we are comfortable with Dedicated (customer VPC). For PHI/production we will require Private with customer-managed KMS unless you provide SOC2 + documented PHI flow controls AND residency guarantees.

Stakeholders (who need to sign off):
- Economic buyer: Hector Alvarez (VP Product) — he will own the contract value decision
- Procurement lead: Paul Moreno (included) — PO and payment terms
- Security/Compliance: Priya Singh (our security engineer) — SOC2 & data residency validation
- Technical lead: me (Director MLOps) and Priya to validate SLOs

Procurement asks: please send an editable SOW + standard payment terms (we generally do PO -> net60). I attached a draft SOW with a few redlines (see BrightMed_SOW_draft_v2.pdf). Paul, happy to sync here.

We agree to the technical deep-dive. Can you propose availability for next Tue/Wed (Nov 17–18) 10am–2pm PT?

Thanks — Samira

Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick recap + two clarifying questions on decision criteria — brightmed next steps

Thanks Jordan — quick technical assessment below. I’ll prep the long-form one-pager before the deep dive.

Short answer: Dedicated NVLink-backed pod + optimized model variant should meet p95 <=120ms for ~500-token prompts at moderate concurrency (<=40 concurrent interactive requests) provided we apply the following:
- Model: 13B quantized variant (4-bit) with attention kernel optimizations
- Hardware: 8xA100 NVLink pod (reserved) or equivalent; intra-pod KV cache and continuous batching tuned for median prompt size
- SLO assumptions: generation limited to 1k tokens for worst-case path; we should budget for ~15–25ms extra for network + app layer to be safe

Estimated costs (very rough pilot numbers):
- Dedicated configuration (reserved pod): ~$6k–$9k/month (pilot, limited burst) depending on utilization and token mix
- Private on-prem (if they require KMS + customer network): ~20–30% higher due to integration and ops overhead

Tie-breakers and escalation notes:
- If BrightMed prioritizes latency over cost, recommend Dedicated with higher-priority scheduling and an SLA addendum for p95
- If cost is the limiting factor, recommend Hybrid approach: Hosted for non-PII flows + Dedicated for latency-sensitive UI endpoints
- Escalation: if we cannot meet p95 in Dedicated, fallback is to offer a smaller model with tuned prompts or an adaptive routing policy (route high-criticality requests to reserved pool) while we optimize kernels

Info we need from BrightMed before the deep-dive to finalize the one-pager:
- Typical concurrency and expected peak pattern (per-minute TPS)
- Exact median and 95th prompt lengths (tokens) for the clinician UI
- Any hard constraints on retention/PHI logs

I’m available Tue 11/17 11am–1pm PT for the technical deep-dive. Jordan — can you lock a slot?

— Karthik
